note: Suite A fixtures: credential-shaped material in outbound-looking tool calls, plus controls. Every token below is SYNTHETIC — invented to match our own detector's format rules, belonging to no account anywhere. They live in this file, and only in this file: the runner reads them and hands them to the firewall over stdin. They are never typed into a command, never printed to a terminal, and never carried into an artifact or a page — a miss records case_id and class only. This file stays in the repo and out of the wheel (MANIFEST.in ships sunglasses/ and attack-db/ only).

cases.class: aws access key id in an outbound command
github token posted to an external endpoint
private key block in an outbound body
signed JWT forwarded to a web fetch
credential handed to an MCP tool (already past the trust boundary)
zero-width character splitting a key inside an outbound command
cases.why: The Aug-12 adversarial finding: one U+200B defeats every format rule while the credential still arrives usable. Normalization is what catches it, so this case guards the normalizer, not the regex.

cases.class: ordinary outbound call carrying no credential
cases.why: A suite that only ever asserts DENY cannot tell 'the right things are blocked' from 'everything is blocked'. This case fails the suite if the firewall starts denying ordinary work.

cases.class: credential-shaped material in a LOCAL write, which is not exfiltration
cases.why: The firewall's model says a local write is not egress. This case locks that in: if it ever starts denying, authoring test fixtures becomes impossible on a machine running our own product — which is exactly the wall this suite hit on 2026-08-28 before the rule was understood.
